resolutions.resolution: change spec so instead of 1st set child we use the body element concept
irc: <ydaniv> oriol: the overflow spec, explaining propagation of value to viewport, says impl. should pick the first from the element based on some conditions
<ydaniv> ... was trying a test case in the issue, according to spec overflow should be propagated from the second body
<ydaniv> ... it seems to be what HTML says as the body element of the document
<smfr> q+
<ydaniv> ... I think we should change spec to do what impl.s do
<astearns> ack smfr
<ydaniv> smfr: does this affect real pages? or theoretical?
<ydaniv> oriol: I think it  won't have much effect, but detectable
<ydaniv> astearns: is the suggested change just removing that sentence?
<ydaniv> oriol: spec should refer to the body element concept, instead of the "1st set child element"
<ydaniv> astearns: other opinions or questions?
<ydaniv> PROPOSED: change spec so instead of 1st set child we use the body element concept
<ydaniv> astearns: obejctions?
<ydaniv> RESOLVED: change spec so instead of 1st set child we use the body element concept

resolutions.background: `calc-size()` can accept all the sizing keywords as its first argument, plus the keyword `any`. But what does `any` mean? It took me awhile (and reorganizing the spec) to figure it out.
irc: <ydaniv> fantasai: have a lot of trouble understanding the any keyword, does it have a basis with other bases
<ydaniv> ... my current proposal for a new name is none
<TabAtkins> q+
<astearns> ack TabAtkins
<ydaniv> TabAtkins: the reaason for any is to indicate the calculation part, which is any size
<ydaniv> ... don't care much about the actual name
<ydaniv> ... fantasai suggests none which I'm ok with
<ydaniv> fantasai: I think it makes it clear that you can't use the calc-size because there's no basis
<weinig> q+
<ydaniv> astearns: other opinions?
<fantasai> s/calc-size/size keyword/
<astearns> ack weinig
<ydaniv> weinig: would that work with the max-size use of none?
<ydaniv> TabAtkins: no
<estelle> q+
<astearns> ack estelle
<ydaniv> estelle: I thought it would be more understanable to use auto
<ydaniv> fantasai: auto means the basis is auto, can't use that
<fantasai> calc-size(basis, size * 3 + 100%)
<ydaniv> TabAtkins: yes, agree
<TabAtkins> (agree that "auto" is already taken, that is)
<ydaniv> fantasai: when you set it to this keyword you can use the size in your expression
<fantasai> s/3/3px/
<fantasai> s/3px/3/
<ydaniv> ... you can't put size because there's no basis, it can't be calc'ed
<ydaniv> ... so this is why I'm proposing none
<astearns> ack dbaron
<ydaniv> dbaron: I'm a little worried about weinig's issue, that we'll never want to use the none of max-size and max-width
<JoshT> q+
<ydaniv> ... since none is a value, and when you learn what calc-size is, so it looks like you're using none as tha basis
<kizu> q+
<ydaniv> TabAtkins: the confusion seems valid, but don't have a strong opinion
<astearns> ack JoshT
<ydaniv> JoshT: I think it's a good keyword, but maybe null?
<ydaniv> TabAtkins: because we don't use null
<astearns> ack kizu
<lea> +1 to no new syntax
<weinig> q+
<ydaniv> kizu: do we need a keyword at all? Could we just use the value?
<ydaniv> TabAtkins: current spec requires 2 values
<ydaniv> dbaron: I think when we added interpolate-size it became more useful?
<ydaniv> TabAtkins: first argument can be the calc, and also the second, so it's not clear if you omit one
<ydaniv> ... you can take an existing calc, remove 2nd arg... so won't to keep a keyword there to reduce confusion
<astearns> ack weinig
<ydaniv> weinig: wanted to clarify, none is not a valid word for min-width, only for max
<TabAtkins> calc-size(50% + 10px, 50% + 10px) is valid, for example, so it's not clear that calc-size(50% + 10px) is meant to treat that as the *second* argument
<fantasai> PROPOSED: Change any to none
<fantasai> +1
<ydaniv> astearns: objections?
<dbaron> I think I lean against but I don't object.
<JoshT> +1
<ydaniv> RESOLVED: change any to none

resolutions.resolution: Adopt 50% currentColor for border-color, assuming we adjust it for special contrast requirements
resolutions.background: We are using mixes of `currentColor` and `transparent` to indicate various form control states. However, the coloration is based on using `border-color: currentColor` as the default state, whereas our survey of design systems showed that common authoring practices tend to use more muted shades of gray rather than black or undiluted currentColor.
irc: <emilio> fantasai: pulled out a bunch of the dependent discussions, this is now about the border-color-ish part of the issue
<emilio> nicole: Wanted to start with basic border-color
<emilio> ... most design systems use a really light border-color
<emilio> ... around 50% of the text color and below
<emilio> ... they didn't set those relative to each other
<emilio> ... value that's here is based on those pieces of data
<emilio> ... gov.uk is the only exception that uses border-color: currentcolor
<emilio> ... but that is the only design system where they do paged forms and so on
<emilio> ... which allows them to be more noise it
<emilio> ... the 50% of currentcolor allows to both lighten and darken, and also allows states to come forward
<emilio> ... let me try to find the value exactly
<kbabbitt> scribe+ kbabbitt
<kbabbitt> emilio: what's the value you're proposing
<kbabbitt> ... ?
<fantasai> select, input, textarea { border: 1px solid color-mix(currentColor 50%, transparent);   /* previously 100% */
<fantasai> }
<keithamus> q?
<masonf> Hopefully 50% not 55%.  I know it doesn't matter, but 55 sounds really opinionated.
<emilio> keithamus: I'd be interested to see the difference between this and bare currentcolor
<emilio> ... I get the argument that design systems are using this
<emilio> ... I just wonder if the complexity of the value is worth it vs. using currentColor
<emilio> ... given our prediction that design systems are going to just change it
<emilio> ... we could use currentColor, I think that's currently what chrome does
<emilio> s/.../jensimmons
<emilio> jensimmons: the problem is that you miss visual hierarchy
<emilio> ... it's much better user experience specially for some users
<emilio> ... having different shades communicates more clearly what's happening
<emilio> q+
<emilio> nicole: while design systems might change it the vast majority might not if we're within that 50/55% range
<emilio> ... they might leave it or change it to a slightly different gray
<astearns> ack emilio
<keithamus> q+
<kbabbitt> emilio: one nice thing about leaving it currentColor is that it works automatically with other things like forced colors etc.
<kbabbitt> ... I would imagine someone who has prefers-contrast would want the black border
<miriam> q+
<kbabbitt> ... agree 80% of users would be better served with shade, but there's some beauty in keeping it simple
<kbabbitt> ... no strong opinion, wouldn't object necessarily
<emilio> nicole: we did actually make forced-colors mode darker
<emilio> ... we use white and black for everything
<emilio> ... in some cases making the border lighter
<emilio> q+
<masonf> q+
<kbabbitt> emilio: but forced colors and prefers-contrast are different right?
<kbabbitt> jensimmons: we should support both
<kbabbitt> emilio: but that means the default ... that increases the complexity of author overrides also, right?
<emilio> jensimmons: I think sometimes I hear folks articulating the idea that having a well thought of design system
<emilio> ... means that the UA styles are more complex
<emilio> ... it's true that it's more complex for browsers to test
<emilio> ... but the idea that it's more complex for authors I'm not sure
<emilio> ... having larger UA styles that change on these modes
<fantasai> Note, prefers-contrast and forced-colors is covered in https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/14318
<emilio> ... IMO it makes it easier for authors
<emilio> q+
<emilio> ... if they want to do that then they'll do that
<emilio> ... if they don't and they forget
<fantasai> Data on border colors https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/14254#issuecomment-5597398476
<emilio> ... or forgot increase contrast, the fact we've taken care of that is a bonus
<emilio> astearns: agreed browser complexity and testing is not a consideration but in some cases more CSS in the UA sheet can make it worse
<emilio> ... in particular it is less to override
<emilio> jensimmons: to be clear I think there's a way for UA sheets can get too complicated for authors
